trace.code: grpc_core::FrameProtector frame_protector_;  // EMBEDDED BY VALUE inside Impl
self->read_mu_.Lock();  // reclaimer callback dereferences the freed FrameProtector (UAF)

preconditions: The gRPC server uses TLS (SecureEndpoint) with ResourceQuota/memory-owner accounting enabled (the default for secure endpoints).
A benign ResourceQuota memory-reclamation sweep is triggered (memory pressure) and pops the reclaimer handle right before the connection's Shutdown() calls memory_owner_.Reset() — a race window.
The owning SecureEndpoint::Impl is destroyed while the reclaimer callback (which captured [self = Ref()]) is still in flight.
In the vulnerable code, ~Impl() destroys frame_protector_ IN PLACE without decrementing the refcount, so the in-flight callback's Ref() points at freed memory.

evidence.vulnerable_version: every release through v1.85.4 (tagged 2026-11-21, commit ee6c9342); the fix 7f3d9778 merged 2026-11-17 is NOT an ancestor of v1.85.4
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased (main only; 7f3d9778 not in v1.85.4 or any earlier tag)
evidence.observed_result: poc.cc transcribes the verbatim vulnerable/fixed lifetime graph (RefCounted vs InternallyRefCounted, OrphanablePtr, ReclaimerQueue::Handle::Orphan, MemoryOwner::Reset) and drives it against a deterministic bump arena that poisons freed blocks with 0xDE. Vulnerable path: the sweep pops the reclaimer handle, Shutdown() -> memory_owner_.Reset() cannot cancel it, ~Impl() destroys frame_protector_ IN PLACE (refcount stays 2), the Impl block is freed+poisoned, and the in-flight callback's self->read_mu_.Lock() reads 0xDEDEDEDEDEDEDEDE instead of the 0x47525043 GRPC magic -> GRPCGHOST-UAF-CONFIRMED. Fixed path: ~Impl() -> OrphanablePtr -> FrameProtector::Orphan() -> Unref() (refcount 2 -> 1) keeps the object alive on the heap, the callback reads the intact magic (GRPCGHOST-FIXED-NO-UAF), and its Ref() is the last reference so the FrameProtector is freed exactly once after the callback completes (GRPCGHOST-FIXED-CLEANUP).

real_exploit.target: grpc/grpc — src/core/handshaker/security/secure_endpoint.cc FrameProtector (RefCounted<FrameProtector>, embedded by value @ v1.85.4 ee6c9342) with MaybePostReclaimer/Shutdown, and the fixed InternallyRefCounted + OrphanablePtr<FrameProtector> @ 7f3d9778
real_exploit.backend: a faithful C++ transcription of the exact vulnerable/fixed lifetime graph (RefCounted vs InternallyRefCounted, OrphanablePtr::Orphan->Unref, ReclaimerQueue::Handle::Orphan cancelling only a still-queued callback, MemoryOwner::Reset), compiled with zig c++ and run against a deterministic arena that poisons freed blocks (0xDE) — turning the ASan-reported heap-use-after-free into an observable, deterministic vulnerable-vs-fixed differential
real_exploit.demonstrated: On the vulnerable path the reclaimer callback dereferences a freed FrameProtector: self->read_mu_.Lock() observes the poison 0xDEDEDEDEDEDEDEDE where the GRPC magic 0x47525043 should be, proving the [self = Ref()] captured pointer outlived its (in-place destroyed) object. On the fixed path the OrphanablePtr/Orphan->Unref keeps the object alive until the callback's Ref() drops, no poison is observed, and the FrameProtector is freed exactly once.
